chunks: Ibn Bukayr narrated from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: We pass with property by the tax collectors, and they ask us to swear an oath to them, and they let us go on our way, and they are not satisfied from us except with that.
He said: Then swear to them, for it is more halal than dates and butter.

key_terms.سَبِيلَنَا: our way; being allowed to pass onward
key_terms.ٱلتَّمْرِ: dates, mentioned as a comparison for lawfulness
key_terms.ٱلزُّبْدِ: butter, mentioned as a comparison for lawfulness
key_terms.ٱلْعُشَّارِ: tax collectors who levy dues on people and goods

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to swear an oath to oppressive tax collectors in order to avoid harm?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about swearing an oath under pressure from tax collectors in order to avoid harm and proceed safely. Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits it emphatically, indicating its lawfulness in such a coercive circumstance.
